info.title: Hearthsound native API
info.description: The control plane of a Hearthsound server. Audio is streamed through the Subsonic surface at /rest.

get.summary: Lists acquisitions across every user, newest first.
get.description:
`state=active` (the default) lists the acquisitions that still hold work,
`state=recent` the ones that ended, and `state=all` both. The ledger is
filtered and paged in memory, so a long-lived server with a large ledger
pays for the full read on every page.

# Errors

Answers `forbidden` for a caller who is not an administrator,
`invalid-request` for an unknown `state` or a malformed cursor, and
`internal` when the ledger cannot be read.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description:
`active` (the default) for acquisitions that still hold work,
`recent` for ones that ended, or `all` for both.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows to answer, 1 to 200; 50 when absent.

post.summary: Cancels an acquisition that still holds work.
post.description:
The worker is stopped and any side effects are undone; the row ends
`cancelled`.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown id and `conflict` when the acquisition
has already ended.

post.summary: Starts a new attempt for a failed or cancelled acquisition.
post.description:
The attempt is a forced request for the same track, so a track cooling
down after its failure is tried again. The caller's permission and daily
quota apply.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown id, `conflict` when the acquisition is
not failed or cancelled or the track is already available, and
`permission-denied` or `quota-exceeded` when the administrator may not
acquire or has spent the day's allowance.

202.description: A new attempt was started or joined

403.description: Not allowed to acquire, or over quota

409.description: The acquisition cannot be retried now

get.summary: Lists the scanned library folders.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `forbidden` for a caller who is not an administrator.

200.description: The folders; `lastScanAt` and `lastScanError` say how the last scan ended

post.summary: Adds a library folder, owned by one account or generic, and scans it.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` when neither or both of `owner` and `generic` are
named, the owner is unknown, the path is not an absolute existing directory,
or the path is `/`, is one of the server's own files or directories, contains
one, or sits inside one; and `conflict` when the folder is already added.

201.description: The new folder; its first scan is queued, and `lastScanError` says how it ended

400.description: No association, an unknown owner, or an unusable path

delete.description:
The folder's file records and the tracks only it held go with it, exactly as
a scan's pruning removes a file the folder lost; a track that still has a
file in the library or the cache stays. The tracks' likes and playlist entries
go with them, and so does their play history. Nothing inside the folder on
disk is removed, moved or renamed, and the folder's watcher stops. Preview the
loss with `GET /api/v1/admin/folders/{id}/removal-impact` first; the web
client does.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown folder.

patch.summary: Changes a folder's name, watch, or association.
patch.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown folder and `invalid-request` for a
contradictory or unknown association.

get.summary: Counts what removing a folder would take with it.
get.description:
The counts describe the delete before it happens: the tracks only this folder
held, and among them the likes and playlist entries that go with them. The web
client asks for them before it sends the delete.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown folder.

200.description: The counts a removal would take with it

post.summary: Queues a scan of one folder.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown folder.

get.summary: Lists every layer with the instances assigned to it.
get.description:
A layer nothing is assigned to is reported with an empty list, so an
administrator sees every layer the server can drive.

# Errors

Answers `internal` when the instance rows or the assignments cannot be read.

put.description:
The body is a JSON array of instance slugs, first is primary; an empty array
leaves the layer with nothing assigned. Every instance must exist and its
plugin must provide the layer.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a body that is not an array of strings,
`not-found` for a slug that names no instance, `invalid-layer` for a layer
this server cannot drive or an instance whose plugin does not provide it,
and `internal` when the assignment cannot be written.

422.description: The layer or an instance cannot serve it

get.summary: Lists the registered plugin repositories.
get.description:
Each repository reports whether it is queried, whether its index is verified
against a configured public key, and the time and error of its last fetch.

# Errors

Answers `internal` when the repository rows cannot be read.

post.summary: Registers a plugin repository.
post.description:
The repository is queried for its index from then on, and its index is
verified against `publicKey` when one is given.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a malformed body, `repositories-disabled` when
`plugins.allow_third_party_repositories` is off, `conflict` when another
repository is registered under the same URL, and `internal` when the row
cannot be written.

409.description: A repository is registered under this URL already

delete.description:
Plugins installed from the repository keep their rows; only the repository
itself goes.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown repository and `internal` when the row
cannot be removed.

patch.description:
The URL is not mutable: a different URL is a different repository. An absent
field keeps its stored value; `null` clears the name or the public key.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown repository, `invalid-request` for a
malformed body, and `internal` when the row cannot be read or written.

get.summary: Lists the installed plugins.
get.description:
Each plugin reports its state, the permissions its manifest requests with
their risk labels, and the newer version the last completed update check
found.

# Errors

Answers `internal` when the plugin rows or a stored manifest cannot be read.

post.summary: Installs a plugin from an index or a repository URL.
post.description:
The plugin is installed with the permissions its manifest requests and
enabled; a newer version of an installed plugin replaces it unless it
requests permissions the installed version does not hold, in which case it
is staged for review. An install with `source` `index` reads the
official index, or the repository `repositoryId` names; an install with
`source` `url` registers the repository at `url` when it is new, which
`plugins.allow_third_party_repositories` gates.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a malformed body, `not-found` for an unknown
repository or plugin id, `conflict` when the version is already installed or
older than the installed one, `repositories-disabled` when a new third-party
repository may not be added, `signature-invalid` when an index's signature
does not verify, `integrity-failed` when an archive is not what the index
declares, `index-unavailable` when an index or archive cannot be
downloaded, `invalid-plugin` when an archive is not a plugin this server can
host, and `internal` when the tables cannot be read or written.

201.description: The plugin was installed, or its upgrade was staged for review

409.description: The version is already installed or older

422.description: The archive is not a plugin this server hosts

502.description: The index or the archive could not be used

get.summary: Lists every plugin the reachable indexes offer.
get.description:
A source that cannot be read is reported in `errors` and does not stop the
listing, so one unreachable repository cannot hide the others.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a malformed repository id, `not-found` for a
repository id that names no row, and `internal` when the repository rows
cannot be read.

parameters.name: repositoryId
parameters.description: The repository to list, `pr_...`; every source when omitted.

200.description: The installable plugins and the sources that failed

post.summary: Reads an uploaded `.hsplugin` file and reports what it holds.
post.description:
The file is staged in the plugins directory, read, and removed again; the
plugin is not installed and nothing is recorded. `provides` lists the layers
the manifest declares and `requestedPermissions` lists what it asks for with
the risk label of each entry, so an administrator can see the permissions
before installing the archive. `plugins.allow_sideload` gates the route.

# Errors

Answers `sideload-disabled` when uploading a plugin is switched off,
`invalid-request` when the body is not multipart, has no `file` part or is
malformed, `invalid-plugin` when the file is not a plugin this server can
host, and `internal` when the file cannot be staged.

400.description: The body is not multipart, has no `file` part, or is malformed

422.description: The file is not a plugin this server hosts

post.summary: Installs a plugin from an uploaded `.hsplugin` file.
post.description:
The request is `multipart/form-data` with one `file` part. The file is staged
in the plugins directory, installed as a sideloaded plugin with the
permissions its manifest requests and enabled, and the staged file is
removed whichever way the install ends. A newer version of an installed
plugin replaces it unless it requests permissions the installed version does
not hold, in which case it is staged for review. `plugins.allow_sideload`
gates the whole route.

# Errors

Answers `sideload-disabled` when uploading a plugin is switched off,
`invalid-request` when the body is not multipart, has no `file` part or is
malformed, `conflict` when the version is already installed or older,
`invalid-plugin` when the file is not a plugin this server can host, and
`internal` when the file cannot be staged or the tables cannot be written.

201.description: The plugin was installed, or its upgrade was staged for review

400.description: The body is not multipart, has no `file` part, or is malformed

409.description: The version is already installed or older

422.description: The file is not a plugin this server hosts

get.summary: Reports one installed plugin.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown plugin and `internal` when the row or its
stored manifest cannot be read.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin id from its manifest

delete.summary: Removes a plugin with its rows, assignments and files.
delete.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown plugin and `internal` when its files
cannot be removed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin id from its manifest

post.summary: Applies a plugin's staged upgrade.
post.description:
The plugin switches to the new version, which replaces the permissions the
installed version holds, and the files of the old version are removed.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown plugin and `conflict` when the plugin has
no staged upgrade.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin id from its manifest

post.summary: Discards a staged upgrade and keeps the installed version in service.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown plugin and `conflict` when no upgrade is
staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin id from its manifest

post.summary: Switches a plugin off.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown plugin.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin id from its manifest

post.summary: Switches a plugin on.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown plugin.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The plugin id from its manifest

get.summary: Lists the configured provider instances.
get.description:
Each instance reports its plugin, its configuration (with the sealed
placeholder in place of every secret), whether it is enabled, and the
outcome of the last health check.

# Errors

Answers `internal` when the instance rows cannot be read.

post.summary: Configures a provider instance from an installed plugin.
post.description:
The plugin must be installed and enabled, the slug must be free, the
server-scoped configuration must satisfy the plugin's schema, and the plugin
must accept it in `lifecycle.validate-config`. The instance is enabled, so
it takes part in the layers it is assigned to.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a malformed body or a slug that is not a
legal slug, `conflict` when the slug is taken, `invalid-provider` when the
plugin is unknown or disabled, provides no layer this server drives, or
rejects the configuration, and `internal` when the plugin cannot be loaded
or the row cannot be written.

201.description: The instance was configured and enabled

422.description: The plugin or the configuration cannot be used

get.summary: Reports one configured provider instance.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown instance and `internal` when the row or
its configuration cannot be read.

delete.description:
The instance's key-value rows and its layer assignments go with it, and the
registry is rebuilt so it stops serving.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown instance and `internal` when the row
cannot be removed.

patch.description:
The configuration is validated and sealed exactly as it is on creation, and
the registry is rebuilt so the change is in service before the answer is
sent. An update that echoes the sealed placeholder back keeps the stored
secret; a write-only field the update leaves out is gone.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a malformed body, `not-found` for an unknown
instance, `invalid-provider` when the plugin rejects the configuration or
cannot serve it, and `internal` when the row cannot be written.

get.summary: Runs one instance's health check.
get.description:
The probe is the plugin's own `lifecycle.health`, run through the first
provider the instance holds. Its outcome is recorded on the instance, so the
provider views report it until the next check.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown instance, `conflict` when the instance is
not in service - it is disabled, or no layer it serves has been assigned to
it - and `internal` when the probe's outcome cannot be recorded.

409.description: The instance is not in service

get.summary: Lists every registered server setting.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `forbidden` for a caller who is not an administrator.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator

patch.summary: Changes server settings; `null` removes a stored value.
patch.description:
Every change is checked before any is written. A key the configuration
file or an environment variable pins is refused with a `conflict` problem
naming all such keys; an unknown key or a value that does not fit is an
`invalid-request` problem. Either way nothing changes.

# Errors

Answers `forbidden` for a non-administrator, `invalid-request` for an
unknown key or invalid value, and `conflict` for pinned keys.

200.description: Every registered server setting after the change

403.description: The caller is not an administrator

409.description: A setting is pinned by the configuration file or the environment

get.summary: Reports what the managed roots and the scanned folders hold.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `internal` when the usage cannot be counted or a policy setting
cannot be read.

post.summary: Runs one maintenance pass now: autopin, relocation, then eviction.
post.description:
The pass is the same one the background worker runs, so it waits for a
pass already in progress and then reports what this one changed.

# Errors

Answers `internal` when a step of the pass fails; the steps after the
failing one do not run.

200.description: The pass ran; what it changed

get.summary: Lists the accounts, a page at a time, by username.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `forbidden` for a caller who is not an administrator and
`invalid-request` for a cursor this server did not issue.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows to answer, 1 to 200; 50 when absent.

post.summary: Creates an account.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for an empty username or password, `conflict`
for a taken username, and `forbidden` for a caller who is not an
administrator.

get.summary: Reads one account.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown account.

delete.description:
The account's sessions, keys, playlists, feedback, ratings and quota go with
it through the foreign keys; a folder it owned becomes generic and the files
it uploaded keep their rows without an uploader. The files on disk are not
touched.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown account, and `conflict` when the caller
would delete their own account.

409.description: The deletion would lock the server out

patch.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown account, `invalid-request` for an empty
password, and `conflict` when administrators would remove their own
administrator flag or disable themselves.

409.description: The change would lock the caller out

post.summary: Signs in with the account password and starts a web session.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` for a wrong username or password (or a disabled
account), `rate-limited` once the address or the username spent its
failure budget, and `internal` when the session cannot be stored.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set

post.summary: Ends the request's web session and clears the cookie.
post.description:
A request authenticated by an API key has no session to end and is answered
the same way; the key stays valid.

# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials, `csrf-failed` for a cookie
without the CSRF header, and `internal` when the session cannot be removed.

204.description: Signed out; the session cookie is cleared

get.summary: Answers who the request is, and the session's CSRF token.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials and `internal` when the
account cannot be read.

get.summary: Streams server events to the caller as Server-Sent Events.
get.description:
The stream is authorized by a bearer key, a session cookie, or a `ticket`
query parameter. Each event is forwarded when its audience admits the
caller; administrators see every event. When the `Last-Event-ID` header is
present, events after that id are replayed before the live feed starts. The
response carries a comment keep-alive every 15 seconds.

# Parameters

- `state`: the native state, which holds the event bus and the ticket store.
- `query`: the optional single-use `ticket`.
- `parts`: the request head, from which the credential and the
  `Last-Event-ID` header are read.

# Returns

A `text/event-stream` response that stays open until the server stops.

# Errors

`400 invalid-request` when `Last-Event-ID` is not an unsigned integer
(checked before a ticket is redeemed, so a malformed request does not spend
the ticket). `401 unauthenticated` when the credential or ticket is missing,
unknown, expired, or already used.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The id of the last frame the client received; missed events are replayed after it

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description:
A ticket from `POST /api/v1/events/ticket`, used in place of a bearer
key or session cookie. Redeemed once.

200.description: A text/event-stream of server events; each frame's data is an event envelope

400.description: Last-Event-ID is not an unsigned integer

post.summary: Issues a single-use ticket for the event stream.
post.description:
The ticket authorizes one connection to `GET /api/v1/events` for 60 seconds
and is consumed by that connection, so a client that needs to reconnect
requests a new one.

# Parameters

- `state`: the native state, which holds the ticket store.
- `authed`: the authenticated caller; the ticket acts as this principal.

# Returns

`201 Created` with the ticket token and its expiry.

# Errors

`401 unauthenticated` when the request carries no valid credential.

201.description: A single-use ticket for the event stream

get.summary: Queues a whole collection for the caller's player.
get.description:
One request answers every track of the collection, in the collection's own
order: the library's sort order for `songs`, the like order for `liked`, the
upload order for `uploads`, the playlist's own order, and the artist's play
count order. Nothing is paged and nothing is truncated.

# Parameters

- `authed`: the caller, whose library the collection is read from.
- `state`: the shared services.
- `query`: the source and, optionally, the track to start at.

# Returns

The collection's items, the position of `from` in them (`0` when absent),
and the source.

# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials, `unknown-source` (400) for a
source this server does not offer, `not-found` (404) when the playlist or
artist is unknown or outside the caller's library, `not-in-source`
(404) when `from` is not one of the collection's tracks, and `internal` when
the read fails.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The track id the player starts at; absent starts at the first item

200.description: The whole collection, in its own order

404.description: The playlist or artist is unknown, or `from` is not in the collection

get.summary: Lists the caller's active API keys.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials and `internal` when the keys

200.description: The caller's active API keys, newest first

post.description:

Answers `invalid-request` for an empty name and `internal` when the key
cannot be stored.

201.description: The new key, with its secret

delete.summary: Revokes one of the caller's API keys.
delete.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for a key that is not the caller's or is already
revoked, and `internal` when the key cannot be updated.

404.description: No such key of the caller's

get.summary: Lists the caller's active app passwords.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials and `internal` when the app
passwords cannot be read.

200.description: The caller's active app passwords, newest first

post.summary: Creates an app password for the caller and answers it once.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for an empty name and `internal` when the app
password cannot be stored.

201.description: The new app password, with its secret

delete.summary: Revokes one of the caller's app passwords.
delete.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an app password that is not the caller's or is
already revoked, and `internal` when it cannot be updated.

404.description: No such app password of the caller's

get.summary: Lists the services the caller may link.
get.description:
One entry per enabled instance whose plugin exports `account-link`, ordered
by slug, with the account the caller linked when there is one.

# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials and `internal` when the
instance or link rows cannot be read. Answers `link-failed` when an instance
cannot be asked how it links accounts.

200.description: The services the caller may link

502.description: A service could not be asked how it links accounts

put.summary: Stores the caller's configuration for a service that links by configuration.
put.description:
The configuration is checked against the plugin's user schema, with the
schema's defaults filled in, and the plugin's `verify-account` names the
account before anything is stored. A service that links through its own site
answers `wrong-link-method`.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown or non-linkable slug, `wrong-link-method`
for a browser service, `invalid-config` when the configuration does not match
the schema, `link-failed` when the plugin rejects the configuration or cannot
answer, and `internal` when the link cannot be stored.

409.description: The service links through the browser

post.summary: Starts a browser link and answers the URL to open.
post.description:
The callback the service sends the listener back to carries a single-use
nonce, and the flow is remembered against the caller and the instance for ten
minutes.

# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown or non-linkable slug, `wrong-link-method`
for a configuration service, and `link-failed` when the plugin cannot answer
or refuses to start the flow.

409.description: The service links with a configuration

502.description: The service could not start the flow

delete.summary: Deletes the caller's link to a service.
delete.description:
# Errors

Answers `not-found` for an unknown or non-linkable slug or when the caller
has not linked the service, and `internal` when the row cannot be removed.

404.description: No such linkable service, or not linked

get.summary: Finishes a browser link from the query the service redirected with.
get.description:
The route always answers a redirect to the account menu: `<path>?linked=<slug>`
when the link was stored and `<path>?linkError=<slug>` for a missing, expired
or foreign nonce, or any failure of the plugin.

# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials; every other outcome is a
redirect, because the address is opened in a browser.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The single-use nonce the link started with

get.summary: Lists the settings the caller may override, with the caller's values.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials and `internal` when a value
cannot be read.

patch.summary: Changes the caller's overrides; `null` removes one.
patch.description:
Every change is checked before any is written, so a batch with one bad
entry changes nothing.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for an unknown key, a key users may not
override, or a value that does not fit the setting.

200.description: The caller's overridable settings after the change

400.description: An unknown, fixed, or invalid setting

put.summary: Rewrites the order of a playlist's entries.
put.description:
One request carries the whole new order, so the playlist is never left
half-reordered: every position is written in one transaction, the entries
keep the instant they were added, and the playlist's `changed` timestamp
moves to now.

# Parameters

- `authed`: the caller, who must own the playlist.
- `state`: the shared services.
- `id`: the playlist's client id (`pl_...`).
- `body`: the new order.

# Returns

`204 No Content` once the order is stored.

# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials, `not-found` (404) when the id
names no playlist or belongs to another account, `invalid-order` (400) when
`order` is not a permutation of the playlist's positions, and `internal`
when the write fails.

400.description: The order is not a permutation of the playlist's positions

404.description: No playlist with that id belongs to the caller

post.summary: Appends a whole album, playlist or artist to a playlist.
post.description:
The source is resolved exactly as `GET /api/v1/library/queue` resolves it:
through the caller's personal library, in the collection's own order. A
catalog album id is materialized first, which is what an album result of a
search carries, and its whole tracklist is appended in provider order.

The edit applies the same playlist pin and the same
`library.acquire_on_playlist_add` step as an edit through `updatePlaylist`,
so a missing track that a user keeps in a playlist is acquired at priority
`queue`.

# Parameters

- `authed`: the caller, who must own the playlist.
- `state`: the shared services.
- `id`: the playlist's client id (`pl_...`).
- `body`: the collection to append.

# Returns

How many tracks were appended and how many the playlist holds afterwards.

# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials, `not-found` (404) when the
playlist, album, playlist source or artist is unknown or outside the
caller's library, `unknown-source` (400) for a source this route does not
accept, and `internal` when a read, materialization or write fails.

200.description: The tracks the request appended and the playlist's size

400.description: The source is not one this route accepts

404.description: The playlist, or a collection in the source, is unknown to the caller

get.summary: Reports whether the server still needs its first administrator.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `internal` when the users table cannot be read.

200.description: Whether the setup is still open

post.summary: Creates the first administrator from the setup link.
post.description:
# Errors

Answers `conflict` when an account already exists, `invalid-request` when
the username or the password is empty, `rate-limited` once the setup
failures spent the budget of the client address or of the `setup` key,
`unauthenticated` when the token is not the one the server logged, and
`internal` when the account cannot be created.

201.description: The administrator exists and is signed in

400.description: The username or the password is empty, or the username breaks the name rule

401.description: The setup link is not valid

409.description: The server already has an account

get.summary: Answers what this server is and what it offers.
get.description:
# Errors

Answers `unauthenticated` without credentials and `internal` when a setting
cannot be read.

200.description: The server's version, features and layers

get.summary: Lists the audio files the caller uploaded, newest first.
get.description:
Only the caller's own uploads are listed: a track that entered somebody
else's library by being uploaded, saved or liked is not theirs to see here.

# Parameters

- `authed`: the caller, whose own uploads are listed.
- `state`: the shared services.
- `params`: the page size and the cursor of the previous page.

# Returns

`200 OK` with one page of uploads.

# Errors

Answers `invalid-request` for a cursor this server did not issue and
`internal` when the library cannot be read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows to answer, 1 to 200; 50 when absent.

200.description: One page of the caller's uploads, newest first

400.description: The cursor is not one this server issued

post.summary: Accepts one or more audio files into the caller's library.
post.description:
The permission and the `uploads.enabled` setting are checked before any
part is read. A file over `uploads.max_file_bytes` ends the request with
`too-large`; files completed before it stay in the library. A file the
library does not index answers as a failed entry instead of an error, so
the other files of the request still land.

# Parameters

- `authed`: the caller, who must hold `can_upload`.
- `state`: the shared services.
- `headers`: the request headers; `Content-Length` sets the total.
- `request`: the multipart body.

# Returns

`201 Created` with one entry per `file` part.

# Errors

Answers `permission-denied` (403) when uploads are off or the account may
not upload, `invalid-request` (400) when the body is not multipart, has no
`file` part or is malformed, `too-large` (413) when a file is over the
limit, and `internal` (500) when the library cannot take a file.

201.description: The files were received; each entry says what became of it

400.description: The body is not multipart, has no `file` part, or is malformed

403.description: Uploads are off, or the account may not upload

413.description: A file is larger than uploads.max_file_bytes
